t.16.1: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purity of being, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, charity, self-restraint and sacrifice, study of the scriptures, austerity, and uprightness.
t.16.2: Non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranquility, absence of slander, compassion toward all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and steadiness.
t.16.3: Vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice, and absence of excessive pride: these, O Bhārata, belong to one born to the divine endowment.
t.16.4: Hypocrisy, arrogance and excessive pride, anger and harshness too, and ignorance, O Pārtha, belong to one who is born to the demonic endowment.
t.16.5: The divine endowment is considered to lead to liberation, the demonic to bondage. Do not grieve, Pāṇḍava; you are born to the divine endowment.
t.16.6: There are two kinds of created beings in this world, the divine and the demonic. The divine has been described at length; now hear from me, O Pārtha, about the demonic.
t.16.7: Demonic people know neither what is to be done nor what is to be refrained from; neither purity nor good conduct nor truth is found in them.
t.16.8: They say that the world is without truth, without foundation, without a Lord, not brought about by any orderly causation; what else is it but caused by desire?
t.16.9: Holding fast to this view, these lost souls of little understanding, doers of cruel deeds and enemies of the world, rise up for its destruction.
t.16.11: Clinging to immeasurable anxiety that ends only with death, holding the enjoyment of desires as the highest aim, they are convinced that this is all there is.
t.16.10: Taking refuge in insatiable desire, filled with hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, having seized upon false notions through delusion, they act with impure vows.
t.16.12: Bound by hundreds of fetters of hope and wholly devoted to desire and anger, they strive by unjust means to amass hoards of wealth for the gratification of their desires.
t.16.13: "This has been gained by me today; this desire I shall attain. This wealth is mine, and this too shall be mine again."
t.16.14: That enemy has been slain by me, and I shall slay others too. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer; I am accomplished, mighty, and happy.
t.16.15: "I am wealthy and of noble birth; who else is there equal to me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice": thus they speak, deluded by ignorance.
t.16.16: Bewildered by many thoughts, enveloped in the net of delusion, and attached to the enjoyment of desires, they fall into a foul hell.
t.16.17: Self-conceited, obstinate, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices that are sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and without regard for the prescribed rules.
t.16.18: Given over to egoism, force, arrogance, desire and anger, these malicious ones hate Me, who dwell in their own bodies and in the bodies of others.
t.16.19: Those hateful and cruel ones, the vilest of men, the inauspicious, I perpetually hurl into the cycles of rebirth, into demonic wombs alone.
t.16.20: Having fallen into demoniac wombs, deluded birth after birth, never attaining Me, O Kaunteya, they then go to the lowest state.
t.16.21: Threefold is this gate of hell, destructive of the self: desire, anger, and likewise greed. Therefore one should abandon these three.
t.16.22: A man who is released from these three gates of darkness, O Kaunteya, practises what is good for himself, and thereby he goes to the supreme goal.
t.16.23: He who casts aside the injunctions of scripture and acts according to the impulse of desire attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme goal.
t.16.24: Therefore let scripture be your authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Having known the action declared by the ordinances of scripture, you should perform it here in this world.
